title: Relics and images deferred; of faith that Saints may be invoked—yet not necessary that each Catholic actually invoke them (Holden)
source_text: LXXVII. Porro ad honorem Sanctorum in Ecclesia Romana, maxime facere videtur cultus qui defertur eorum reliquiis, & imagines quae illorum locis sacris statuuntur, & variis modis coluntur, sed ista speciali disputationi reservare visum est. Hic solum monendum superest rem quidem esse de fide in Ecclesia Romana, ut credamus Sanctos licite & pie invocari posse: caeterum fatentur non esse necesse, ut fideles singuli Sanctos orent & invocent: posse enim aliquem ad salutem pervenire, Deum per Christum invocando, absque tali invocatione. Ut videre est apud Henricum Holden de resolutione fidei lib. 2. cap. 7. Profitemur quidem, inquit, posse Sanctos haud inutiliter invocari: sed teneri Catholicos omnes ad actuale hujusmodi invocationis exercitium, nullatenus tanquam veritatem Christianam asserimus. Poterunt namque salvari, imo & reipsa salvantur forsan aliqui Catholici, qui Sanctos in caelo coronatos nunquam invocaverunt.
pass_a_gloss: Further, to the honor of the Saints in the Roman Church, the cult which is paid to their relics, and the images which are set up in their sacred places and are cultivated in various ways, seems to contribute most, but it has seemed good to reserve those things for a special disputation. Here only this remains to be warned: that it is indeed a matter of faith in the Roman Church that we believe that the Saints can be licitly and piously invoked: yet they confess that it is not necessary that individual faithful pray to and invoke the Saints: for someone can arrive at salvation, invoking God through Christ, without such invocation. As may be seen in Henry Holden on the resolution of faith, book 2, chapter 7. We profess indeed, he says, that the Saints can be invoked not unusefully: but that all Catholics are bound to the actual exercise of this kind of invocation we by no means assert as Christian truth. For some Catholics will be able to be saved, nay perhaps are in fact saved, who have never invoked the Saints crowned in heaven.
pass_b_english: Relics and images matter most for Saint-honor but are reserved for a later dispute.
Of faith: Saints may be licitly invoked—yet not that every Catholic must actually invoke them.
Holden: invocation is useful, not a binding actual duty; some Catholics are saved who never invoked Saints.
Romana closes at LXXVII; next frontier is Pars Secunda (Reformata).
